result.summary: Probed RSS + JSON Feed generation exhaustively (dozens of builds). Spec at /tmp/probe/findings/feeds.md, artifacts at /tmp/probe/artifacts/feeds/. FORMAT - RSS is ONE LINE, no indentation, NO trailing newline, no BOM. Prologue exactly: `` Only `xmlns:content`. No atom:link, ttl, language, docs, enclosure, isPermaLink. - channel order: title, link, description, pubDate, lastBuildDate, generator(=`marmite`), items. Channel title/description are ALWAYS the global site name/tagline — never per-tag/author/series/stream. - item order: title, link, [description], [author], [category]*, guid(==link), pubDate, source, content:encoded. `{feed basename}` on every item. - pubDate: `%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT` (year zero-padded to 4: `0999`). lastBuildDate = build time in UTC, TZ-independent. - JSON: 2-space pretty, no trailing newline. version = `https://jsonfeed.org/version/1`. Keys: version,title,home_page_url,feed_url,description,items; item keys: id,url,title,content_html,summary,date_published,image,authors,tags,language. date_published = `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S-00:00` (literal MINUS 00:00). BIGGEST SURPRISES - ``/`summary` contain the description in a QUOTED form: `"` + s with `\`→`\\`, `"`→`\"` + `"`, but newlines/tabs/control chars left literal (so NOT JSON encoding). Non-string YAML gives `null`, `42`, `3.14`, `true`, `["a", "b"]`. Missing key ⇒ element omitted / `summary:""`. - Item cap is 15, hard-coded (pagination has no effect) — for every feed kind. - SERIES feeds are sorted ASCENDING (oldest first) and keep the oldest 15; all other feeds descending. Channel pubDate = FIRST item after ordering+capping, so it's the OLDEST date in a series feed. - RSS uses the protocol-normalized url (`example.com`→`http://example.com`, empty→`http://`); JSON Feed uses the RAW config url (empty→`home_page_url:""`, `feed_url:"/index.json"`). Trailing `/` not stripped ⇒ `//`. - `draft: true` posts and future-dated posts ARE in feeds. Pages (no date) never are. - Only the FIRST author gets ``, as the raw key (not display name). - XML escaping includes `'`→`'` and `>`→`>`. `]]>` in CDATA split as `]]]]>`. - JSON `image` precedence: card_image (emitted QUOTED, e.g. `"\"media/c.png\""`) > banner_image (raw) > first `` src > `""`. - An author declared in marmite.yaml WITHOUT `avatar:` crashes list.html rendering, so author-*.rss/.json are never written. - No posts ⇒ zero feed files. index.rss is only the `index` stream's feed.
surprises: Feed item cap is a hard-coded 15, unaffected by `pagination`; applies to RSS and JSON and every feed kind (tag/author/series/stream/archive).

Series feeds are sorted ASCENDING by date (oldest 15 kept), unlike every other feed which is descending — and the channel <pubDate> is therefore the OLDEST date for series feeds (rule: date of first item after ordering+capping).

<description> (RSS) and "summary" (JSON) hold a 'quoted' form of the front-matter description: wrap in double quotes, escape only backslash and double-quote; newlines/tabs/control bytes stay literal. Non-string YAML values become `null`, `42`, `3.14`, `true`, `["a", "b"]`. This same quoted string is what HTML meta tags use with `"` chars stripped.

RSS uses the protocol-normalized site url (empty ⇒ `http://`, so links look like `http:///post.html`), but the JSON Feed uses the RAW config url (empty ⇒ home_page_url "" and feed_url "/index.json"). Trailing slash is never stripped, producing `//` in links.
`draft: true` is not honoured anywhere — such posts appear in feeds (and can supply the channel pubDate). Future-dated posts are also included.
Only the FIRST author is emitted as <author>, and it is the raw front-matter key (e.g. `bruno`), not the configured display name; `default_author` fills in only when the post has no authors at all.
XML escaping covers 5 chars including `'`→`'` and `>`→`>`; control chars (\n,\t,\r,\x01) are written raw into element text. `]]>` inside CDATA is split as `]]]]><![CDATA[>`.
JSON `image` uses card_image FIRST (and emits it in the quoted form `"\"media/c.png\""`), then banner_image raw, then the first src in the rendered content.
An author entry in marmite.yaml lacking `avatar:` makes list.html rendering fail (`url_for` Missing `path`), which aborts the render step and means author-*.rss / author-*.json are never produced.
index.rss is nothing more than the feed of the stream named `index`; if all posts are in other streams no index.rss is written, and a site with only pages produces no feed files at all.
`<generator>` is the bare string `marmite` with no version, and there is no atom:link/self, ttl, language, or guid isPermaLink attribute.

Tie-broken item order follows the filesystem readdir() order of the content directory (stable sort), so it is deterministic per directory but not portable; `pinned: true` reorders HTML but not feeds; `updated:` never affects pubDate.
